transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-02
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Ethan Park (Marlow Head of Search), Lena Ortiz (Marlow ML Eng), Tom Black (CTO)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood Inference, AE on the account. Priya our solutions engineer is here to run the embeddings + reranker hosted flow and show console traces. How's that sound?
[00:06] Ethan: Sounds good. We have about 40 minutes. I'm Ethan, I own search at Marlow. Quick context: we're replacing a hybrid BM25 + neural reranker, currently using in-house embeddings and Elastic for vector store. We're exploring whether to move embeddings + rerank to hosted Redwood for simplicity.
[00:20] Jordan: Great. Priya, take it away, we can jump into the API demo then talk cost/latency.
[00:24] Priya: Cool, thanks. I'll share my screen — give me a sec. Okay, so first quick note: the demo will show the embeddings endpoint for dense vectors, then a reranking call pattern using the hosted reranker endpoint that accepts candidate docs + query vectors. We'll also look at the Console where you can see per-request token cost, latency, and trace ids.
[00:44] Priya: (typing sounds) Alright, showing a small curl example — we're calling POST /v1/embeddings with model redwood-embed-22-large, passing text payloads. Response returns vectors of dim 1024, base64 encoded in this example. In practice the libraries return floats array.
[01:05] Lena: Wait, quick Q — does the embeddings endpoint support batching? We usually send 256 queries at once during indexing jobs.
[01:10] Priya: Yes, batching is supported. The hosted endpoint allows batch sizes up to X (depends on model); for redwood-embed-22-large we recommend 64-128 per request to balance memory on the server. For large bulk ingestion we suggest the bulk ingestion helper in the Console which does paging and parallelization.
[01:26] Tom: And what about vector normalization? We do cosine at rank time. Do you normalize server-side?
[01:30] Priya: We return raw vectors; you can choose normalization client-side or pass a flag to the reranker to treat embeddings as cosine-similarity. The reranker endpoint accepts 'metric: cosine' parameter. Small caveat: if you use quantized variants in Dedicated, norm behavior changes slightly — we'll put that in the notes.
[01:48] Jordan: On the reranker — high level it's an HTTP endpoint where you POST query + candidate docs (IDs + text or embeddings) and get back reranked list and scores. Works well when you have a shortlist from Elastic.
[02:03] Priya: I'm switching to the Console now — here's the request tracing UI. You can see this sample request id. Traces show token count, model latency, and cost breakdown per token. This is handy if you want to find heavy prompts or long contexts.
[02:25] Ethan: Nice. Do traces show batch-level breakdowns too?
[02:28] Priya: Yes, for batched requests the trace will show the internal batching window and per-subrequest latencies. Helps debug latency spikes that come from long tail sequences.
[02:40] (short crosstalk)
[02:45] Lena: Can we restrict logs? We have strict PII rules.
[02:48] Jordan: Good call. We have request-level redaction and retention policies; by default hosted retains minimal metadata and no raw payload unless you opt in for longer retention. We also have Private deployment for customers who require VPC or on-prem with customer-managed KMS.
[03:04] Tom: Does Redwood host the vector DB? We currently use Elastic vectors plus our own sharding.
[03:08] Priya: Redwood doesn't require you to change your vector store. Our typical pattern is: keep Elastic or Pinecone for nearest-neighbor search, call embeddings endpoint for vectors, use nearest neighbor to produce ~50 candidates, then call the reranker to re-score with the model. That keeps costs down because reranker only processes shortlist.
[03:29] Jordan: Let's go through a small example. I'll call a pretend query — 'best merchant account for B2B payroll' — and show the pipeline.
[03:36] [05:00] (demo running, sample HTTP requests shown, short pauses)
[05:05] Priya: Here is the reranker request body: it takes query text, optional query vector, and candidates array. Each candidate can be just id + text or id + precomputed embedding. If you pass embedding we skip the internal embed step. The response returns 'ranked_candidates' with score and explain fields.
[05:30] Lena: Are explain outputs deterministic? We need to audit reranker decisions.
[05:35] Priya: The explain snippets are deterministic given same inputs and model version; but note that some stochastic sampling options exist if you enable them (we keep sampling off by default for reranker calls). We also store model version in the trace.
[05:50] Ethan: Performance numbers? We need 200 qps at 200ms p95 for reranking 50 candidates.
[05:58] Priya: For hosted, 200 QPS reranking 50 candidates is a mid-range load — depends on model size. For redwood-rerank-compact we often see p95 under 120-180ms at 200qps with continuous batching. If you need stricter SLOs we recommend Dedicated pools with reserved GPU capacity — that gives predictable tail latency. I can share a spreadsheet with throughput estimates by model and candidate size.
[06:25] Tom: How does batching interact with latency? We can't add 100ms if batch waits accumulate.
[06:29] Priya: Our runtime uses adaptive batching with tight latency SLO enforcement. There's a tunable 'max batching window' and 'preferred latency' you can set per-route. Optimize will suggest batch configs based on observed distribution. For aggressive throughput you accept some latency increase. For strict p95 you pin to smaller batch windows or dedicated capacity.
[06:50] Jordan: I'll drop that Optimize config note in the follow-up.
[06:55] (pause)
[07:00] Ethan: Security — we need SOC2 and ISO type compliance. Any concerns for hosted?
[07:05] Jordan: We published SOC 2 Type II summary and ISO certs for our control plane — I'll share the cert links. For high-reg customers we do Private with VPC peering and customer KMS. Also, audit logs are available per token.
[07:20] Lena: Any PII redaction?
[07:22] Priya: We offer request redaction rules in Console and can wire an automated preprocessor to remove PII. For POC, you can scrub before sending vectors.
[07:33] Ethan: Cost — what's the delta if we rerank 50 candidates per query vs re-ranking top10?
[07:38] Priya: Cost scales roughly linearly with input tokens and candidates processed. If you switch from 50 to 10 candidates you'll see ~5x lower token processing on rerank. Also consider passing precomputed embeddings to the reranker to save embedding token cost. Optimize can recommend a candidate cutoff for maximal NDCG per cost.
[07:56] Jordan: We can run a quick offline sim with your sample dataset to recommend an optimal shortlist size.
[08:02] Ethan: That would be helpful.
[08:05] (demo continues, showing Console Optimize suggestions)
[08:12] Priya: Here's the Optimize tab — it flags high-cost prompts and suggests quantized model variants or batching thresholds. For embeddings-heavy ingestion it suggested using redwood-embed-22-small for near-duplicate detection and redwood-embed-22-large for semantic search.
[08:32] Lena: How hard is switching models in production? We want model pinning for rollouts.
[08:36] Priya: It's first-class — you can pin model versions per route and do canary rollouts in Console. There's automatic fallback to a cheaper model on overload if you opt into multi-model routing.
[08:50] Tom: Any penalties in output quality when using quantized models? We've seen small drops.
[08:54] Priya: Yes, quantization reduces FP precision — for reranking that's usually acceptable for most thresholds but we surface quality regressions via evals. We'll run your eval set and report delta.
[09:06] Jordan: Let's talk about the POC scope: quick plan — ingest 5k docs, produce embeddings, build a nearest-neighbor shortlist in your Elastic, run Redwood reranker on held-out queries, compute NDCG and latency. Priya, anything to add?
[09:20] Priya: We'll supply ingestion scripts, a sample reranker client, and a small evaluation harness. For the POC we recommend 2-week run: first week ingest + smoke tests, second week run production-like load and gather metrics.
[09:34] Ethan: Timeline — we're aiming for an internal decision by end of March. So quick turnaround is needed.
[09:40] Jordan: Sounds feasible. We'll prioritize sample throughput numbers and the POC kickoff calendar.
[09:45] (short silence)
[10:00] Lena: One more technical: does reranker support per-candidate metadata like publication date, click signals? We want to incorporate business features.
[10:06] Priya: Yes, candidates accept a metadata dict; you can pass numeric features and we can concatenate them into the scoring prompt or the reranker can accept structured features as inputs. There is a size limit on prompt tokens obviously, so large metadata should be encoded or pre-bucketed.
[10:22] Tom: Any thoughts on cold-start indexing? We have a lot of historical docs.
[10:25] Priya: For cold-start, batch embeddings is the path. Use Optimize suggestions to pick a smaller embedding model for cheap initial indexing then re-embed hot documents with higher-quality model. Also, use prefix/KV caching for popular queries to save cost.
[10:40] Ethan: Great. Can you also include a sample SLA for Dedicated? Our legal team will want numbers.
[10:45] Jordan: Yes, I'll include the Dedicated SLA PDF.
[10:48] (some background noise)
[11:00] Priya: Recap of deliverables — we'll send: pricing spreadsheet, POC ingestion scripts, security docs, sample reranker client, and a recommended shortlist size via offline simulation.
[11:12] Ethan: Perfect. Any blockers from our side?
[11:15] Tom: We'll need legal to review SOC2 and decide if hosted is acceptable. For now we'll start with hosted POC and escalate to Private if required.
[11:25] Jordan: Great. Quick final Qs?
[11:28] Lena: No other Qs. Thanks, that was really helpful.
[11:31] Jordan: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with those artifacts and schedule the kickoff.
[11:35] (meeting ends)

Transcript notes: occasional mis-transcriptions (model names sometimes garbled in audio), some overlapping speech markers missing. References: security doc (link shared in chat), POC guide (attachment), pricing spreadsheet (will be shared).
